messages.author: 56168e3bb7011f27
messages.subject: Non-stationary anisotropic code
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to fit a non-stationary anisotropic model with INLA to my (spatial R^2) data. I am using rgeneric and I was wondering whether there is any experimental code available to get the G1 and G2 matrices for the precision matrix Q. 

Thank you in advance!

Isa

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Non-stationary anisotropic code
parts:
I think you are looking for
?inla.mesh.fem
(this is not experimental, but has G1 G2 etc)

Note that there are several non-stationary models that have been developed before. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06350

Best,
Haakon

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Non-stationary anisotropic code
parts:
Hi,
There is some ill-documented methods for obtaining building blocks needed for some types of locally anisotropic models. (Undocumented since they were part of as-yet-unfinished research)

This is in addition to the inla.mesh.fem function; those matrices are mainly useful for nonstationary but locally isotropic models.

Whether a combination of the above can be used for your model depends on the details of what model you want to implement. 

Finn
